title: When to involve a qualified person

sections.skill: Recognize when a qualified person must review the answer

questions.prompt: Which question most needs a qualified person to review the answer?

choices.text: Whether two medicines are safe together
How to format a bulleted list
Synonyms for the word "quick" in a story
Ideas for a birthday card

questions.correct_answer: Whether two medicines are safe together
questions.intro: Some questions carry HIGH STAKES: health and medicine, legal rights and court matters, large money decisions, safety (electrical work, chemicals, driving), and decisions about other people's well-being. For these, an AI answer can help you prepare: understand terms, make a list of questions, organize your documents. But a QUALIFIED PERSON who is accountable, such as a doctor, pharmacist, lawyer, licensed electrician or financial counselor, should review the actual decision, because they can examine your specific situation and take responsibility. In an emergency, contact emergency services directly.

sections.skill: Compare AI help with a recipe versus surgery

questions.prompt: Why is a failed recipe low stakes?

choices.text: Food never matters
You can try again with little harm
Recipes are always perfect the first time
Recipes are illegal

questions.correct_answer: You can try again with little harm
questions.intro: If a recipe goes wrong, you get a bad dinner and try again tomorrow: LOW STAKES and easy to reverse. If surgery goes wrong, the harm can be serious and permanent: HIGH STAKES. You might read about either online, but you would never let a website perform surgery. AI answers fit the same pattern: fine to rely on for low-stakes, reversible things you can check, but for high-stakes decisions about health, law, money or safety, a qualified, accountable person should be involved.

sections.skill: Weigh stakes, sources and access to qualified help

questions.prompt: Three sources disagree about whether a supplement is safe with a prescription. What does this signal?

choices.text: Pick the most popular answer
Assume it is safe
Ask a pharmacist or doctor
Take half the dose

questions.correct_answer: Ask a pharmacist or doctor
questions.intro: Deciding when to involve a qualified person is itself a skill. Signs that you need one: the answer depends on facts about your body, your documents or your location; being wrong could cause injury, legal trouble or a large loss; or different sources disagree. Signs that an AI answer may be enough: low stakes, easy to reverse, and checkable yourself. Cost and access can be real barriers, so look for free or low-cost qualified help, such as pharmacists, legal aid clinics, school counselors or nonprofit credit counselors.
questions.feedback: Disagreement on safety means ask a qualified person.
